title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
This is an impersonation and interface-spoofing failure, not a failure of the trading app. The app is described as legitimate. What was fabricated was the screen the victim was reading, a ghost site built by a third party that displayed investment information not tied to the real account. Trust was built on small investments that genuinely showed returns and could be withdrawn, which made the later fabricated figures look like a working system.

The failure sits at the presentation layer, the point where a user reads the state of an account. Nothing inside the genuine service was altered, so no check performed within the app could have surfaced the substitution. Catching it would have required confirming the account's state through a channel the attacker did not control.

What is not established is any wrongdoing by the app's operator, any charge or verdict against the person who made contact, or the recovery of the funds. The police account describes an investigation still in progress, and the reporting describes recovery in these cases as rare rather than impossible.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired couple from Georgia lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started when a stranger contacted Jerry Dunaway through WhatsApp. The scammer convinced Jerry to invest money using a mobile trading app, and initial small investments showed returns, allowing him to withdraw funds and build trust. Over time, Jerry invested increasingly larger amounts, but when he attempted a larger withdrawal last week, the funds became inaccessible. Police discovered that although the trading app was legitimate, scammers had created an artificial ghost site that displayed fake investment information on his screen.

Jerry and Mindy Dunaway are now warning others about the sophisticated tactics used by the scammers. Gwinnett County police are investigating the case, but authorities indicate that victims in these situations rarely recover their stolen money. The couple's children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help them cover daily living expenses as they work to recover from their financial loss.
